key_insight: Early structural signals in hidden neurons, captured by the Overfitting-Underfitting Indicator (OUI), reliably predict whether a PPO actor–critic run with a given learning rate will converge, collapse, or underfit—often within the initial training steps—enabling early intervention.
problem_solved: Addresses PPO's extreme sensitivity to learning rate and the expensive, time-consuming hyperparameter search by providing an early indicator of run stability and eventual performance.
method: Compute the Overfitting–Underfitting Indicator (OUI) from hidden neuron activations during the first training epochs of PPO actor–critic runs.
Correlate OUI trajectories across a range of learning rates with long-term outcomes (convergence, collapse, slow learning) to identify reproducible structural signatures.
Use the early OUI signal to classify runs as stable/unstable and propose interventions (early stop, LR reduction or increase, or reinitialization) to avoid wasted compute.
impact: Enables practitioners to detect unstable or doomed PPO runs early, reducing wasted compute and accelerating hyperparameter tuning; improves reliability of RL training by informing learning-rate choices and automated interventions.
visual_elements: Timeline plot: early OUI trajectory (first epochs) overlaid with final return to show predictive power.
Heatmap: hidden-neuron activation patterns across different learning rates, highlighting structural differences for collapse vs successful runs.
Scatter plot: learning rate vs final performance colored by early OUI classification (stable / underfitting / collapsing).
Flowchart: suggested workflow — measure OUI early → classify run → apply intervention (stop / adjust LR / continue).
paper_title: When Learning Rates Go Wrong: Early Structural Signals in PPO Actor-Critic
paper_authors: Alberto Fernández-Hernández, Cristian Pérez-Corral, Jose I. Mestre, Manuel F. Dolz, Jose Duato
